title: Social Network Game Development
one_liner: A mobile-first social gaming market built around free-to-play apps, creator platforms, live operations, virtual goods and in-game advertising.
overview: The 2022 IBISWorld baseline placed US Social Network Game Development revenue at $5.1 billion in 2021 and projected $6.9 billion in 2026, equal to a 6.3% 2021-2026 CAGR. Since then, the market has become less dependent on games embedded directly in Facebook-style social networks and more tied to mobile games, multiplayer social loops, Roblox-style creator economies, Discord/TikTok-driven discovery, live events, social casino mechanics and hybrid in-app purchase plus advertising monetization. Public 2025-2026 data point to a mature but still large demand base: US total video game consumer spending reached $60.8 billion in 2025, US mobile game demand reached $26.7 billion in 2025, and global mobile game IAP revenue reached $82 billion in 2025. Growth is now driven more by retention, live operations, payer conversion, content cadence, creator payouts and direct-to-consumer payment channels than by first-time smartphone adoption.

key_stats.market_size: 2026 US industry revenue: about $6.9 billion, using the 2022 IBISWorld 2026 forecast for Social Network Game Development.
key_stats.growth: 2021-2026 baseline CAGR: 6.3%; 2025 US mobile game consumer spending growth: 1.0%; 2025 US total video game consumer spending growth: 1.4%.
key_stats.demand_benchmark: 2025 US mobile game consumer spending: $26.7 billion; 2025 US total video game consumer spending: $60.8 billion; 2025 US video game content spending: $52.4 billion after March 2026 restatement.
key_stats.global_mobile_context: 2025 global mobile game IAP revenue: $82 billion, up 1.0% from 2024, with 52 billion total game downloads across mobile, PC and console in 2025.
key_stats.profit_margin: 2026 baseline EBIT margin forecast: 19.7% of revenue, up from 19.3% in 2021.
key_stats.businesses: 2026 baseline enterprises forecast: 3,212 companies, up from 2,630 companies in 2021.
key_stats.employment: 2026 baseline employment forecast: 13,211 workers, up from 9,951 workers in 2021.
key_stats.concentration: 2026 concentration remains medium: large publishers and platforms set monetization norms, while small studios and creator teams still enter through app stores and user-generated-content platforms.

baseline_2022.market_size: 2021 US industry revenue: $5.1 billion in the January 2022 IBISWorld baseline; 2026 forecast revenue: $6.9 billion.
baseline_2022.growth: 2016-2021 revenue CAGR: 9.8%; 2021 revenue growth: 6.9%; 2021-2026 forecast CAGR: 6.3%.
baseline_2022.establishments: 2021 establishments: 2,697; 2026 forecast establishments: about 3,355 if applying the baseline 2021-2027 establishment CAGR of 4.47%.
baseline_2022.product_mix: 2021 revenue mix: puzzle games 22.1%, gambling-style social casino games 17.2%, role-playing games 14.3%, strategy games 13.8%, other games 32.6%.

how_it_makes_money: Revenue comes from optional in-game purchases, virtual currency, season passes, subscriptions, advertising, rewarded video, offerwalls, brand integrations, licensing, creator marketplace fees, platform commissions, direct-to-consumer web stores and live-service content drops. Most titles are free to download, so studios optimize payer conversion, average revenue per user, retention cohorts and paid user acquisition payback periods.
cost_structure: The largest costs are software engineering, game design, art production, cloud hosting, platform fees to Apple, Google, Roblox and other distribution platforms, creator or developer payouts, user acquisition, influencer and performance marketing, analytics, trust and safety, content moderation, customer support, payment processing and corporate overhead. Public 2025 filings show the model clearly: Playtika spent $949.8 million on sales and marketing in 2025 and derived 66.3% of 2025 revenue through Apple and Google billing systems, while Take-Two generated 97.0% of fiscal 2026 revenue through digital online channels.
major_players: Take-Two Interactive/Zynga: fiscal 2026 net revenue was $6.66 billion, mobile revenue was $3.33 billion and recurrent consumer spending was $5.20 billion.
Roblox: 2025 revenue was reported at $4.9 billion, 2025 bookings at $6.8 billion, 2025 average DAUs at 127 million and 2025 creator earnings above $1.5 billion.
Playtika: 2025 revenue was $2.76 billion, with 2025 casual games at 70.8% of revenue and social casino-themed games at 29.2%.
Electronic Arts: fiscal 2026 net revenue was $7.53 billion and live services and other revenue was $5.38 billion, supported by EA SPORTS FC Mobile and other connected communities.

Microsoft Gaming/King: Candy Crush remained a top US mobile grossing title in 2024, and King remains a major operator in casual social mobile games after Microsoft’s 2023 Activision Blizzard acquisition.
Scopely: MONOPOLY GO! ranked as the top grossing US mobile game in 2024 and remains a major benchmark for social casual monetization in 2025-2026.
current_dynamics: The industry is in a post-hypergrowth phase. Player time is still high, but installs are harder to buy profitably, privacy limits have reduced targeting precision, and more revenue comes from existing live titles rather than brand-new games. Mobile remains the anchor platform, but Roblox and other UGC ecosystems are shifting some value from traditional studios to creator networks. Social casino is still profitable, but 2025 Playtika disclosures show pressure in legacy social casino titles, including a 23.2% 2025 decline in its social casino-themed games portfolio. The strongest operators use first-party data, live events, direct-to-consumer payments, IP collaborations, creator payouts and cross-platform communities to protect margins.
whats_growing: Growing areas include multiplayer casual games, puzzle and party games, Roblox and UGC experiences, rewarded ads, hybrid-casual monetization, direct-to-consumer web stores, creator economies, branded live events, TikTok-driven discovery, live operations teams, AI-assisted content production and mobile games with strong social loops. US mobile game demand rose to $26.7 billion in 2025, and 67% of Americans ages 5-90 played video games at least one hour per week in 2026 ESA research.
whats_shrinking: Shrinking or pressured areas include Facebook-canvas-style social games, weakly differentiated hypercasual games, social casino titles with aging payer cohorts, new launches that rely only on paid user acquisition, games without live-service cadence, and titles exposed to Apple/Google platform fees without direct payment alternatives. Playtika reported that 2025 social casino-themed game revenue declined 23.2%, while Sensor Tower reported 2025 global mobile game revenue grew only 1.0%, signaling maturity rather than broad category acceleration.
recent_developments: 2025-07-31: Roblox reported Q2 2025 revenue of $1.08 billion, bookings of $1.44 billion and 111.8 million average DAUs, then raised 2025 guidance.
2026-02-11: ESA, Circana and Sensor Tower reported 2025 US video game consumer spending of $60.7 billion, later restated in March 2026 to $60.8 billion.
2026-02-26: Sensor Tower reported 2025 global mobile game IAP revenue of $82 billion, up 1.0% from 2024, and 52 billion total game downloads across platforms.
2026-02-26: Playtika reported 2025 revenue of $2.76 billion, 2025 DTC platform revenue of $814.5 million and a 23.2% decline in 2025 social casino-themed game revenue.
2026-05: Take-Two reported fiscal 2026 net bookings of $6.72 billion, with recurrent consumer spending at 78% of total net bookings and mobile revenue of $3.33 billion.
2026-06-03: ESA reported that 67% of Americans ages 5-90, or more than 212 million people, played video games at least weekly in 2026.
outlook: Revenue should keep expanding modestly through 2026-2028, but growth will be slower and more uneven than the 2016-2021 period. The best-positioned developers will own durable franchises, social graphs, creator tools, direct payment relationships and strong live-ops capabilities. Smaller studios can still break through, but the cost of discovery and retention makes the market less forgiving. Expect consolidation, more licensed IP, more AI-assisted production, more platform scrutiny around minors and payments, and a continued shift from one-off launches toward service businesses with recurring events and virtual economies.
sources: IBISWorld baseline file: social-network-game-development.txt, last updated 2022-01-30
one_sentence: Social network game developers make free-to-play games and shared virtual experiences that use friends, feeds, communities or creator networks to acquire users and monetize them through virtual currency, in-app purchases, subscriptions, ads and platform economies.

title: Social Networking Sites
one_liner: U.S. social networking sites are a scaled, advertising-led digital media industry where growth is shifting from user adoption to AI-driven ad performance, short-form video, creators, social commerce and privacy-safe measurement.
overview: Social networking sites publish and operate platforms that let users build profiles, form networks, share posts, images and video, follow creators and organizations, and interact with communities. The industry remains highly concentrated because scaled platforms have more user data, more content supply, stronger ad measurement, larger creator ecosystems and better AI infrastructure than smaller networks. Advertising is still the core revenue engine, but subscriptions, creator tools, in-app commerce, paid messaging and data or licensing arrangements have become more important. In 2025, U.S. usage was mature rather than explosive: DataReportal counted 253 million U.S. social media user identities in January 2025, equal to 73.0% of the population, and its 2026 report counted 254 million in October 2025, equal to 73.0% of the population. Revenue growth therefore came less from adding new Americans to social media and more from higher ad prices, more impressions, better automated targeting, short-form video monetization, creator campaigns and social commerce.

key_stats.market_size: 2025: $117.7 billion in U.S. social media advertising revenue; 2026: Statista Market Insights projected $126.0 billion in U.S. social media advertising spend.
key_stats.growth: 2025: U.S. social media ad revenue grew 32.6% year over year, adding about $29.0 billion.
key_stats.digital_ad_context: 2025: total U.S. internet advertising revenue reached $294.6 billion, up 13.9% year over year.
key_stats.users: 2025: 253 million U.S. social media user identities in January 2025; 2026 report: 254 million in October 2025.
key_stats.meta_anchor: 2025: Meta reported $74.78 billion of United States revenue and $198.76 billion of Family of Apps revenue globally.
key_stats.profitability: 2025: Meta Family of Apps operating income was $102.47 billion on $198.76 billion of revenue; Reddit 2025 net margin was 24.1%; Snap 2025 remained loss-making with a $460.5 million net loss.

baseline_2022.market_size: 2022: about $73.7 billion, calculated from the baseline IBISWorld 2021 revenue of $62.5 billion and its 2021-2026 projected CAGR of 17.9%.
baseline_2022.growth: 2022: about 17.9% projected growth under the baseline IBISWorld 2021-2026 forecast.
baseline_2022.baseline_context: 2021: IBISWorld reported $62.5 billion of revenue, 23.1% profit margin, 3,344 enterprises and 103,287 employees; it projected 2026 revenue of $142.1 billion.

how_it_makes_money: In 2025, the industry made money primarily by selling targeted display, video, feed, stories, reels, sponsored post and performance ads to marketers. Platforms also monetized through creator marketplace tools, promoted listings, commerce fees, subscriptions such as Snapchat+ and LinkedIn Premium, professional recruiting and sales products, paid messaging, payments fees, data licensing, API licensing and brand safety or analytics tools. Advertising remains dominant: Meta said substantially all of its 2025 revenue came from advertising on Facebook and Instagram, and Snap reported 2025 advertising revenue of $5.19 billion out of $5.93 billion total revenue.
cost_structure: The largest 2025-2026 costs are employee compensation for engineering, trust and safety, sales and product teams; data centers, cloud infrastructure, AI training and inference, content delivery and storage; sales and marketing; content moderation and compliance; payments, partner and creator incentives; depreciation; legal settlements and regulatory response. The baseline IBIS report showed 2021 profit margin of 23.1%, but current margins vary sharply: Meta's 2025 Family of Apps operating margin was about 51.6%, Reddit's 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin was 38.4%, and Snap reported a 2025 net loss as it absorbed infrastructure and product costs.
major_players: Meta Platforms: 2025 United States revenue of $74.78 billion; Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp reached 3.58 billion global daily active people in December 2025.
TikTok/ByteDance: 2025 White House order cited about 170 million American users; TikTok Shop U.S. GMV reached $15.1 billion in 2025, up 68% year over year according to Momentum Works and Tabcut.
Microsoft LinkedIn: Microsoft fiscal 2025 LinkedIn revenue increased 9%, including Talent Solutions, Marketing Solutions, Premium Subscriptions and Sales Solutions.
Snap: 2025 revenue was $5.93 billion, up 11%; United States revenue was $3.4 billion; Q4 2025 DAUs were 474 million globally.
Reddit: 2025 revenue was $2.20 billion, up 69%; U.S. revenue was $1.79 billion, up 68%; Q4 2025 U.S. DAUq was 52.5 million.

Pinterest and X: 2025-2026 competitors for visual discovery, creators, political conversation, brand advertising and performance campaigns, with monetization tied to shopping intent, subscriptions and ad recovery.
current_dynamics: The 2025-2026 market is no longer mainly about getting Americans online; it is about capturing attention, improving ad return and lowering measurement friction in a privacy-constrained environment. AI ad tools are raising pricing and performance for scaled networks, while short-form video and creator-led commerce are pulling budgets from traditional display and some search. Social commerce is becoming a larger strategic wedge, especially on TikTok, Instagram, Pinterest and YouTube-adjacent creator ecosystems. At the same time, state youth-safety rules, age-assurance requirements, privacy litigation and the FTC's continuing Meta appeal increase compliance costs and product risk.
whats_growing: 2025-2026 growth is strongest in short-form video ads, Reels-style inventory, creator advertising, AI-generated creative and targeting tools, social commerce, paid verification and premium subscriptions, professional-network monetization, Reddit-style community advertising, and first-party measurement products. U.S. creator ad spend was projected by IAB at $37 billion in 2025 and $44 billion in 2026, showing how creator-led formats have become core media rather than experimental spend.
whats_shrinking: Growth is shrinking in mature U.S. user penetration, broad undifferentiated feed networks, low-quality display inventory, third-party-cookie and cross-app tracking-dependent measurement, youth-directed engagement features under regulatory scrutiny, and smaller ad-supported networks that lack scale, brand safety tools or commerce attribution. Snap's North America user trends and X's advertiser volatility illustrate the pressure on platforms that must either rebuild trust, improve ad performance or diversify into subscriptions and commerce.
recent_developments: 2025-09-25: The White House issued Executive Order 14352, determining a TikTok U.S. divestiture framework could qualify under the 2024 law and citing about 170 million American TikTok users.
2026-01-20: The FTC filed a notice of appeal after a November 2025 district court ruling favored Meta in the Instagram and WhatsApp monopolization case.
2026-02-05: Reddit reported 2025 revenue of $2.20 billion, up 69%, including U.S. revenue of $1.79 billion, up 68%.
2026-04-16: IAB/PwC reported 2025 U.S. social media ad revenue of $117.7 billion, up 32.6% year over year.
2026-08-06: A New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay an additional $567 million tied to youth mental-health harms, bringing state-trial liability to $942 million, with Meta saying it would appeal.
outlook: The 2026 outlook is positive but more contested. U.S. social networking revenue should keep expanding as advertisers shift budget into social video, creator campaigns, AI-optimized buying and commerce-linked placements, but growth will likely normalize after the 2025 social ad surge. The biggest upside is better ad yield from AI, creator marketplaces and closed-loop shopping. The biggest downside is regulation: youth safety, age verification, app-store accountability, antitrust appeals, privacy rules and national-security oversight of foreign-owned platforms can raise costs or change product design. Large incumbents should remain profitable because they own audiences, data and buying tools, while smaller sites need differentiated communities, subscriptions or commerce niches to survive.
themes: AI-driven ad targeting and creative automation
Short-form video and creator-led media buying
Youth safety, age assurance and platform liability
one_sentence: In 2025, U.S. social networking site economics were anchored by $117.7 billion in social media ad revenue, up 32.6% year over year, while 2026 competition centered on Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Snap, Pinterest, Reddit and X as regulators pressed harder on youth safety, antitrust and data control.

title: Soda Production in the US
one_liner: US soda producers are defending a mature, high-concentration category with pricing, zero-sugar reformulation, flavor innovation and energy-drink exposure as traditional CSD volume remains soft.
overview: This industry manufactures carbonated soft drinks, energy drinks and other artificially carbonated flavored beverages, excluding bottled water, juice, ready-to-drink tea and coffee. The 2022 baseline showed a mature industry under pressure from declining per-capita soft drink consumption, health concerns and soda taxes, partly offset by energy drinks, premium craft sodas and brand extensions. Current 2025-2026 data points to the same split: all-channel US CSD dollars rose in 2025, but volume was flat to down, while energy drinks, functional beverages, flavor-led launches and zero-sugar products supplied the growth engine. Large players remain advantaged by brands, bottling systems, retailer access, procurement scale and pricing power.

key_stats.market_size: 2025 estimated US soda production revenue: about $36.1 billion, based on the 2022 baseline revenue of $36.574 billion and the baseline 2027 forecast of $35.8 billion; Beverage Digest reported 2025 US all-channel CSD dollars up 3.1% and volume down 0.7%.
key_stats.growth: 2025 current-dollar category growth was price-led: US all-channel CSD dollars +3.1% and volume -0.7%; the 2022 IBIS baseline projected 2022-2027 producer revenue CAGR of -0.4%.
key_stats.pricing: BLS/FRED soft drink manufacturing PPI was 344.950 in May 2026 versus 326.897 in May 2025, up about 5.5% year over year.
key_stats.establishments: 2023 Census Business Patterns reported 622 employer establishments for NAICS 312111 soft drink manufacturing.
key_stats.profitability: 2022 baseline industry profit margin was 8.0%; large branded systems show higher segment operating margins, such as Keurig Dr Pepper US Refreshment Beverages adjusted operating income of 29.8% of 2025 net sales.
key_stats.trade: 2022 baseline exports were $1.348 billion and imports were $4.387 billion, with imports supported by foreign-produced energy drinks.

baseline_2022.growth: 2022 revenue declined 0.8%; 2017-2022 revenue CAGR was -3.3%; 2022-2027 forecast CAGR was -0.4%.
baseline_2022.profit: $2.926 billion in 2022 profit, equal to an 8.0% margin.

how_it_makes_money: Producers earn revenue by selling branded and private-label carbonated beverages, concentrates, syrups and finished packaged products through bottlers, wholesalers, supermarkets, convenience stores, mass retailers, restaurants, vending, fountain and foodservice channels. Large systems monetize brands through concentrate sales, direct bottling, distribution agreements, fountain contracts and retailer shelf space; smaller producers rely on premium flavors, natural ingredients, local distribution and specialty retail channels.
cost_structure: Major costs are sweeteners, flavoring syrups and concentrates, aluminum cans, PET bottles, glass, closures, carbon dioxide, water treatment, plant labor, energy, freight, warehousing, trade promotion and marketing. In the 2022 baseline, wages were $3.505 billion, about 9.6% of revenue, and profit was 8.0% of revenue. In 2025-2026, packaging, freight, tariffs and commodity inflation remained key pressure points; PepsiCo cited higher commodity costs and tariffs affecting PBNA operating profit in 2025, while the soft drink manufacturing PPI was up about 5.5% year over year in May 2026.
major_players: The Coca-Cola Company and affiliated bottlers
PepsiCo Inc.
Keurig Dr Pepper Inc.
National Beverage Corp.
Red Bull GmbH and US distributors
Monster Beverage Corp. and strategic distribution partners
Private-label and regional craft soda producers
current_dynamics: Demand is bifurcated. Legacy colas and full-sugar CSDs remain large but mature, with 2025 all-channel volume declining even as pricing lifted dollars. Zero-sugar colas, flavor extensions, mini cans, multipacks, energy drinks and functional beverages are taking share of growth. Large companies are using pricing, packaging architecture and route-to-market scale to protect margins, while smaller brands compete on nostalgia, natural sweeteners, novel flavors and premium positioning. Retailers and foodservice customers continue to matter because fountain, convenience and grocery channels shape volume, promotional intensity and pack mix.
whats_growing: Energy drinks, zero-sugar CSDs, flavored and limited-time variants, premium craft sodas, smaller portion packs, multipacks, functional beverages and brands with strong convenience-store distribution are growing. Keurig Dr Pepper reported 2025 US Refreshment Beverages net sales up 11.9% to $10.4 billion, with growth from energy, CSDs and sports hydration, including GHOST. Beverage Industry/S&D Insights projected 2025 energy drink volume up 9.7%.
whats_shrinking: Traditional full-sugar and diet CSD volumes remain structurally pressured by health concerns, competition from bottled water and functional beverages, and local sugar-sweetened beverage taxes. PepsiCo reported 2025 PBNA unit volume down 3%, including a slight CSD volume decline and a 6% non-carbonated beverage volume decline. Beverage Digest reported 2025 US all-channel CSD volume down 0.7% despite dollar growth.
recent_developments: 2025-06-11: Keurig Dr Pepper released its 2025 State of Beverages report, saying 58% of Americans view CSDs as more refreshing than other beverages and 59% say new flavors motivate beverage trial.
2026-02-03: PepsiCo filed its 2025 Form 10-K, reporting PBNA net revenue of $28.197 billion in 2025, up 1.5%, while PBNA unit volume declined 3% and CSD volume declined slightly.
2026-02-20: Coca-Cola filed its 2025 Form 10-K, reporting 33.8 billion global unit cases in 2025, with sparkling soft drinks at 69% of global unit case volume and 61% of US unit case volume.
2026-02-24: Keurig Dr Pepper reported 2025 US Refreshment Beverages net sales of $10.4 billion, up 11.9%, with market-share gains in CSDs, energy and sports hydration.
2026-04-08: Beverage Digest reported 2025 US all-channel liquid refreshment beverage dollars up 2.5% and volume down 0.9%, while CSD dollars rose 3.1% and CSD volume fell 0.7%.
2026-06-11: FRED/BLS showed the soft drink manufacturing PPI at 344.950 for May 2026, about 5.5% above May 2025.
outlook: The 2026 outlook is for low real growth and continued margin management rather than a broad volume recovery. Dollar sales can keep rising if pricing, premium packs and energy/functional mix offset weaker traditional CSD volume, but health pressure, private-label value seeking, sugar taxes and competition from water, coffee, tea, sports hydration and functional beverages limit upside. The best-positioned operators are those with national distribution, high-velocity brands, zero-sugar credibility, energy-drink exposure and procurement scale in cans, PET, sweeteners and freight.
themes: Energy drinks as the main growth offset
Retail and fountain channel mix normalization
Packaging, tariff and commodity cost pressure
one_sentence: The industry still generates roughly mid-$30-billion producer revenue, but 2025 growth came more from price and mix than volume as consumers shifted toward zero-sugar, energy, functional and flavored alternatives.

title: Soft Drink, Baked Goods & Other Grocery Wholesaling in the US
one_liner: A large, fragmented wholesale channel moving soft drinks, bottled water, baked goods, coffee, canned foods and other shelf-stable groceries from manufacturers to grocers, convenience stores, specialty retailers and foodservice operators.
overview: This industry covers merchant wholesalers of specialized grocery products, including soft drinks, bottled water, bakery products, coffee, tea, spices, cereals, canned foods and other non-frozen, non-fresh grocery items. The 2022 IBIS baseline put industry revenue at $487.9 billion after a 16.0% inflation-driven jump. Using the Census/FRED grocery and related product wholesale sales series as a current proxy, broader NAICS 4244 sales rose from $862.0 billion in 2022 to $949.1 billion in 2025, a 10.1% increase; applying that movement to the IBIS-defined 2022 base implies a 2025 market size near $537.1 billion and a 2026 run-rate near $559.6 billion based on January-May 2026 sales running 4.2% above January-May 2025. The market remains mature and highly competitive, with scale advantages in routing, procurement, data systems and retailer relationships offset by opportunities for specialty, natural, organic, functional beverage and local-brand distributors.

key_stats.market_size: 2026E $559.6B, estimated from the 2022 IBIS revenue base indexed to Census/FRED NAICS 4244 sales through May 2026
key_stats.growth: 2026 YTD +4.2% for Census/FRED NAICS 4244 grocery and related product wholesale sales, January-May 2026 versus January-May 2025
key_stats.2025_proxy_sales: 2025 $949.1B for broader Census/FRED NAICS 4244 grocery and related product wholesale sales, +5.1% versus 2024
key_stats.2025_employment_proxy: 2025 846.3K jobs for broader BLS NAICS 4244 grocery and related product wholesalers, down 0.6% from 2024
key_stats.2026_price_signal: June 2026 PPI for wholesaling of baked goods, non-alcoholic beverages and all other groceries was 162.554, with May 2026 at 181.492, index June 2013=100
key_stats.2026_food_price_context: USDA July 2026 forecast: food-at-home prices +2.7% in 2026 and nonalcoholic beverage prices +3.9% in 2026

how_it_makes_money: Wholesalers buy packaged grocery and beverage products from manufacturers and processors, hold inventory in distribution centers, consolidate mixed orders, and resell cases or pallets to supermarkets, convenience stores, specialty food retailers, warehouse clubs, foodservice operators and institutional buyers. Revenue is driven by case volume, product mix, contract pricing, freight terms, vendor allowances, service fees, private-label programs and the ability to pass through food, packaging and fuel inflation.

cost_structure.purchases: 2022-2026: merchandise purchases are the dominant cost, typically the bulk of revenue, because wholesalers take title to packaged food and beverage inventory before resale.
cost_structure.wages: 2022 IBIS baseline wages were $23.7B, equal to about 4.9% of 2022 revenue; 2025 BLS proxy data show grocery-wholesale employment at 846.3K jobs for broader NAICS 4244.
cost_structure.profit: 2022 IBIS baseline profit margin was 3.8%; 2026 margins remain pressured by fuel, warehouse, insurance, interest and labor costs.
cost_structure.logistics: 2025-2026: trucking, route density, warehouse automation, spoilage control and on-time delivery performance are key cost levers.
cost_structure.technology: 2025-2026: larger operators are spending on demand planning, route optimization, retailer portals, cybersecurity and warehouse scanning to protect service levels and reduce picking errors.

major_players: United Natural Foods Inc. - FY2025 net sales $31.8B, with natural segment sales up 9.2% on a comparable 52-week basis
Sysco Corporation - FY2025 global sales $81.4B, with U.S. Foodservice sales of $57.0B; more foodservice-weighted than the IBIS niche but an important adjacent distributor
KeHE Distributors - major private specialty, natural and organic distributor; announced 2025 long-term renewals with INFRA and Sprouts
C&S Wholesale Grocers - large private grocery wholesaler with scale in supermarket supply and self-distribution services
Jetro Restaurant Depot - cash-and-carry and foodservice wholesale operator serving independent restaurants and small businesses
Regional beverage bottlers and specialty distributors - fragmented local operators remain important in soft drinks, bottled water, bakery routes and specialty grocery categories
current_dynamics: Nominal sales are still rising, but the mix has shifted from pandemic pantry-loading to a split between value-seeking grocery demand and resilient away-from-home foodservice demand. Price inflation is less extreme than 2022, but USDA still forecasts 2026 food-at-home inflation of 2.7% and nonalcoholic beverage inflation of 3.9%, supporting dollar sales while complicating purchasing and contract resets. Larger distributors are using scale, technology and long-term retailer agreements to defend service levels, while smaller specialists compete on local brands, natural and organic assortments, ethnic groceries and high-touch service. Retailer consolidation and self-distribution remain structural threats because large supermarket and club chains can bypass third-party wholesalers for high-volume items.
whats_growing: 2025-2026 functional beverages, energy drinks, protein shakes and hydration products as consumers choose beverages for energy, mood, nutrition and convenience
2025-2026 natural, organic and specialty grocery distribution, supported by UNFI natural segment growth and KeHE retailer renewals
2025-2026 foodservice demand, with the National Restaurant Association projecting 2026 restaurant and foodservice sales of $1.55T
2025-2026 distributor technology spending on route visibility, order accuracy, warehouse scanning and retailer portals
2025-2026 private-label and value-oriented packaged groceries as inflation-sensitive households trade across brands and formats
whats_shrinking: 2025-2026 traditional carbonated soft drink volumes and some legacy packaged dessert categories as health and wellness preferences shift demand
2025-2026 employment intensity in broader grocery wholesaling, with BLS proxy employment down 0.6% in 2025 despite higher nominal output
2025-2026 small wholesalers' pricing power where large retailers can self-distribute or buy direct from manufacturers
2025-2026 unit growth in some conventional grocery categories where dollar growth is led more by price than volume
2025-2026 operating slack, because inventory, fuel, insurance and labor costs keep thin-margin distributors under pressure
recent_developments: 2026-08: Census reported June 2026 total merchant wholesale sales of $794.1B, up 14.1% from June 2025, with inventories/sales at 1.19.
2026-07: USDA forecast 2026 food-at-home prices to rise 2.7% and nonalcoholic beverage prices to rise 3.9%.
2026-07: National Restaurant Association revised its 2026 restaurant and foodservice sales growth outlook to 4.3%, with real growth of 0.8%.
2026-06: BLS/FRED reported 2025 sectoral output for broader NAICS 4244 grocery wholesalers at $1.087T and employment at 846.3K jobs.
2025-09: UNFI reported FY2025 net sales of $31.8B, up 4.6% on a comparable 52-week basis, with natural product sales up 9.2%.
2025-07: KeHE announced a 10-year INFRA contract extension after 141% revenue growth in the partnership since 2019.
outlook: The industry should keep expanding in nominal dollars through 2026-2027, but growth will be more measured than the 2021-2022 inflation spike. The near-term base case is mid-single-digit nominal growth in 2026, supported by grocery inflation, functional beverage demand, specialty grocery growth and resilient foodservice sales. Profitability should remain narrow because customers resist price increases while supplier, freight, wage, insurance and technology costs stay elevated. Consolidation, direct buying by large retailers and self-distribution will continue to pressure undifferentiated wholesalers, while distributors with specialty assortments, dense delivery networks and strong digital ordering tools should gain share.
one_sentence: In 2026, the industry is still growing in nominal terms as grocery and foodservice demand remains resilient, but margins remain thin because product, labor, fuel and warehouse costs move faster than many wholesalers can reprice contracts.

title: Software Testing Services
one_liner: Independent QA, automation and quality engineering providers test the reliability, security and performance of software before and after release.
overview: The US software testing services industry sits between software development, IT consulting and cybersecurity. Demand rises with application complexity, cloud migration, mobile app use, e-commerce, regulated digital workflows and the spread of AI-generated code. The 2020 baseline described a fast-growing but competitive domestic industry, with 2020 revenue of $6.143 billion and pressure from offshore delivery. By 2025-2026, the market has moved further toward quality engineering: testing is increasingly embedded in DevOps pipelines, sold as managed services or testing-as-a-service, and augmented by AI for test-case generation, self-healing scripts, visual validation, defect triage and model evaluation. Labor remains the main cost, but cloud device farms, automation platforms and offshore/nearshore delivery networks are now central to scale.

how_it_makes_money: Providers charge through managed QA contracts, project-based test engagements, staff augmentation, offshore/nearshore delivery teams, subscription access to testing platforms, device-browser clouds, automated regression suites, performance and load testing, security and compliance testing, accessibility testing, user acceptance testing, AI model/application evaluation and consulting tied to DevOps or quality engineering transformation.
cost_structure: Labor is the largest cost, led by QA engineers, SDETs, automation architects, test managers, security testers and offshore delivery teams. Other major costs include cloud infrastructure, device labs, browser and mobile farms, automation and observability tools, sales and customer success, compliance/security controls, recruiting, training and subcontractors. The 2020 baseline had wages of $2.828 billion on $6.143 billion of revenue, or about 46% of revenue, and 6.8% profit margin; 2025 wage data show QA talent remains expensive with a $104,300 US median annual wage.

current_dynamics: Demand is healthy but changing shape. Buyers are still outsourcing repetitive regression testing and cross-device coverage, but the premium work is shifting to AI-enabled quality engineering, security validation, observability, test data management and continuous testing inside CI/CD pipelines. Enterprise clients want faster release cycles and measurable defect reduction, while vendors compete on automation IP, offshore scale, cloud test infrastructure and domain expertise in banking, healthcare, retail, telecom and government. AI-generated code is increasing test volume and uncertainty, creating demand for smarter test selection, model evaluation and risk-based QA, but it also pressures providers to automate their own delivery and defend margins.
whats_growing: AI-assisted and agentic test automation, cloud-based testing platforms, mobile and cross-browser testing, accessibility testing, security and compliance testing, API testing, performance engineering, test observability, managed testing services, quality engineering transformation, AI application evaluation and real-world crowdtesting for digital experiences.
whats_shrinking: Standalone manual functional testing, commodity offshore test execution, late-cycle waterfall QA, on-premise-only test labs, long regression cycles without automation, and low-value staff augmentation contracts where buyers can use internal DevOps teams or AI-assisted tools.
recent_developments: 2025-02-26: BrowserStack launched a unified Test Platform with AI-powered workflows, 20,000+ real devices and 3,500+ browser-desktop combinations.
2025-05-07: BrowserStack acquired Requestly, adding HTTP interception and API mocking capabilities for frontend and test workflows.
2025-06-30: BrowserStack launched BrowserStack AI agents for test planning, authoring, maintenance, accessibility checks and visual reviews, claiming up to 50% productivity gains.
2025-07-23: Tricentis introduced Agentic Test Automation in Tosca, using natural-language prompts to generate automated test cases.
2026-02-03: Gartner forecast worldwide 2026 IT spending of $6.155 trillion, including $1.434 trillion in software spending and $1.867 trillion in IT services spending.
2026-04-15: Applause reported that 55% of surveyed organizations had released AI-powered applications or features, while quality issues such as hallucinations and unreliable outputs were rising.
outlook: The industry should keep expanding through 2026 as enterprises modernize applications, adopt AI coding tools and push more customer, employee and compliance workflows into software. Growth is likely to outpace the older IBIS baseline because software release frequency, cloud-native complexity and AI validation needs have increased. Margins will remain mixed: premium automation, security, regulated-industry and AI-evaluation work can command better rates, while routine functional testing faces price pressure from offshore providers and self-service AI testing platforms. Winning firms will combine domain expertise, automation IP, global delivery and outcome-based quality metrics rather than selling testing hours alone.
one_sentence: Software testing services sell manual, automated, cloud, security, performance, mobile and AI-assisted quality assurance to software publishers, enterprises and government buyers that need faster releases without unacceptable defect, security or compliance risk.
